1.title: Introduction to Calisthenics
1.excerpt: Discover the fundamentals of calisthenics and how to start your training.
1.content:
Calisthenics is a form of training that uses your own body weight as resistance. It is an accessible discipline for everyone, as it requires no expensive equipment or gym memberships. With just your body and some space, you can develop strength, flexibility, and coordination progressively.

The fundamental calisthenics exercises include push-ups, pull-ups, dips, and squats. Each of these movements works multiple muscle groups simultaneously, making workouts efficient and comprehensive. As you progress, you can increase difficulty through more advanced variations.

To get started, we recommend establishing a routine of 3 to 4 days per week, alternating work days with rest days. Begin with the most basic versions of each exercise and progressively increase the difficulty. Consistency is the key to progress in calisthenics.

At OpenCalisthenics, you will find a complete exercise library with detailed instructions and recommended progressions. You can also create your own personalized routines and track your progress over time.

2.title: News: AI Integration for Personalized Routines
2.excerpt: Now you can generate personalized routines with our new AI feature.
2.content:
We are pleased to announce one of the most anticipated features of OpenCalisthenics: artificial intelligence integration for creating personalized routines. This new feature analyzes your goals, experience level, and available equipment to generate workouts specifically tailored to you.

The AI takes into account multiple factors when creating your routine: your current fitness level, the muscles you want to work, the time you have available, and any physical restrictions you may have. The result is a coherent and progressive training plan that adapts to your unique needs.

To access this feature, simply go to the workouts section and select the assisted creation option. Answer a few questions about your goals and preferences, and in seconds you will have a personalized plan ready to use. You can save it, modify it, and share it with other users.

This is just the first phase of our AI integration. In the coming months, we will continue to improve the system with adjustment capabilities based on your progress and feedback.

3.title: Calisthenic Progressions: From Beginner to Advanced
3.excerpt: Learn how to advance your calisthenics exercises with effective progressions.
3.content:
One of the most fascinating aspects of calisthenics is its progression system. Every advanced exercise has a series of stages that allow you to develop the necessary strength and technique gradually and safely. Understanding these progressions is essential for advancing effectively.

Take pull-ups as an example: the journey begins with scapular activation exercises and negative pull-ups, then you advance to band-assisted pull-ups and regular pull-ups, to finally reach weighted pull-ups and the one-arm pull-up. Each step builds upon the previous one.

The same applies to pushing exercises like push-ups: from wall push-ups for absolute beginners, through incline and knee push-ups, to standard push-ups, diamond push-ups, archer push-ups, and finally the one-arm push-up. The key is not to skip stages and to master each level before advancing.

At OpenCalisthenics, each exercise includes its progression tree, showing you the prerequisite exercises and those you will unlock upon mastering it. Use the available roadmaps to plan your learning path and keep track of your progress.

4.title: The Best Resistance Band Exercises: The Periodic Table of Fitness
4.excerpt: Discover 52 of the best resistance band exercises organized by category, with videos and progressions for all levels.
4.content:
Resistance bands are one of the most versatile tools in modern fitness. With a simple piece of latex or rubber, you can work virtually any muscle group, add resistance to classic calisthenics exercises, or use them as assistance in high-difficulty movements like pull-ups. They are lightweight, affordable, and adaptable to any fitness level.

One of the greatest advantages of resistance bands is that they provide variable resistance: the more you stretch the band, the greater the resistance. This means the peak of muscular work occurs exactly where the muscle is strongest, making them an ideal tool for both beginners and advanced athletes. Additionally, since there are no free weights, the risk of injury is considerably lower.

In this article, we have compiled 52 of the best resistance band exercises, organized by the muscle groups they target. From basic core exercises like crunches and Russian twists, to advanced compound movements like thrusters and squat cleans, there are options for every level. Each exercise includes a demonstration video so you can learn the correct technique.

For chest and pushing exercises, the band can be anchored behind you to simulate a chest press, or placed around your back to add resistance to push-ups. Exercises like the chest press, chest fly, and band-resisted push-ups are excellent options for working the chest without machines or dumbbells.

For back training, the band row is the foundational exercise. From there you can progress to lat pulls, high rows, or pull-overs, which work the lats from different angles. These exercises are also excellent preparation for pull-ups, as they strengthen the same primary muscles.

For legs, bands offer a great variety of options. From back and front squats with a band, through lunges in all their variations (lunge fly, lunge press, lunge row) to advanced unilateral movements like split squats or band-assisted pistol squats. Hamstring curls and Romanian deadlifts are also excellent for the posterior chain.

Core training is equally well served. Crunches with a band, Russian twists, oblique twists, and anti-rotation crunches are exercises specifically designed to strengthen the trunk with added resistance. The cross plank with a band works anti-rotational stability, one of the most important yet undertrained aspects of core strength.

Finally, for shoulders and arms, resistance band exercises are particularly useful because they allow you to work in multiple planes and angles. The shoulder press, L raise, deltoid flies, bicep curls with different anchor points, and tricep extensions are among the most effective. Remember that progression is key: start with lighter resistance bands and gradually increase the challenge.

faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know to get started

q1.question: Do I need equipment to start?
q1.answer: For most beginner exercises you only need your body. Some progressions require a pull-up bar or parallel bars, which you can easily find in calisthenics parks or sports facilities.

q2.question: Is it suitable for absolute beginners?
q2.answer: Yes. The app includes progressions from zero: wall push-ups, assisted squats, or incline planks. You can start with no prior fitness background.

q3.question: How often should I train?
q3.answer: We recommend starting with 3-4 days per week, alternating work days and rest days. The app's routines and roadmaps are designed with this in mind.

q4.question: How long until I see results?
q4.answer: With consistency, most people notice improvements in strength and endurance within 2-4 weeks. Visible physical changes typically appear between the first and third month.

q5.question: Is the app free?
q5.answer: Yes, OpenCalisthenics is completely free and open source. You can use all features without restrictions or subscriptions.

1.name: Push Up
1.description: Basic exercise for chest, shoulders and triceps. Get into plank position with hands at shoulder width and lower your body until your chest almost touches the floor.
1.instructions:
Place your hands on the ground at shoulder height, slightly wider than shoulder width
Extend your legs back, supporting yourself on your toes
Keep your body straight forming a line from head to heels
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your chest almost touches the ground
Push up extending your arms to return to the starting position
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement

2.name: Pull Up
2.description: Fundamental exercise for back and biceps. Hang from a bar with overhand grip and pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
2.instructions:
Grab the bar with palms facing forward, hands shoulder-width apart
Hang with arms fully extended and feet off the ground
Retract your shoulder blades and engage your core
Pull your body up bringing your chest toward the bar
Rise until your chin clears the bar
Lower in a controlled manner to starting position with arms extended

3.name: Squat
3.description: Basic squat for legs. Lower your hips as if sitting down while keeping your back straight and knees aligned with your feet.
3.instructions:
Place your feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly pointed out
Keep your chest up and gaze forward
Initiate the movement by pushing your hips back
Bend your knees lowering until thighs are parallel to the floor or lower
Keep your knees aligned with your feet without caving inward
Push through your heels to return to starting position

4.name: Dips
4.description: Parallel bar dips for triceps and chest. Support yourself on parallel bars and lower your body by bending your elbows to a 90-degree angle.
4.instructions:
Grip the parallel bars with arms extended
Keep your core engaged and legs slightly forward or crossed
Lower your body by bending your elbows to a 90-degree angle
Keep elbows close to body for triceps emphasis, or flared for chest
Push up until arms are fully extended
Avoid swinging and control the movement throughout

5.name: Plank
5.description: Isometric plank for core. Keep your body straight supported on forearms and toes, engaging your abs.
5.instructions:
Place your forearms on the ground with elbows under shoulders
Extend your legs back supporting yourself on your toes
Keep your body completely straight forming a straight line
Engage your core by squeezing your abs as if bracing for impact
Don't let your hips rise or drop
Maintain the position while breathing in a controlled manner

6.name: Muscle Up
6.description: Advanced exercise combining pull-up and dip. Perform an explosive pull-up and transition over the bar to complete a dip.
6.instructions:
Hang from the bar with false grip (thumbs over the bar)
Start with a slight swing to generate momentum
Pull explosively bringing your chest to the bar
Rotate your wrists over the bar during the transition
Push up completing a dip over the bar
Lower in a controlled manner to the hanging position

7.name: Pistol Squat
7.description: Single-leg squat. Lower completely on one leg while keeping the other extended forward.
7.instructions:
Stand on one leg with the other extended forward
Extend your arms forward for balance
Slowly lower by bending the supporting knee
Keep your free leg extended without touching the ground
Lower until your glute almost touches your heel
Push through your heel to stand back up

8.name: Handstand Push Up
8.description: Push-ups in handstand position. Perform a push-up while inverted against a wall or in freestanding balance.
8.instructions:
Place your hands on the ground about 6-8 inches from the wall
Kick up to handstand position against the wall with body straight
Keep your core very tight and legs together
Lower your head toward the ground by bending your elbows
Gently touch the ground with your head or lower to 90 degrees
Push up until arms are fully extended

9.name: L-Sit
9.description: Isometric L position. Sit with legs extended and lift your entire body off the ground using only your hands.
9.instructions:
Sit on the ground with legs extended
Place your hands beside your hips with fingers pointing forward
Press hard against the ground and lift your body
Keep your legs straight and parallel to the ground forming an L
Strongly engage your core and hip flexors
Hold the position as long as possible

10.name: Australian Pull Up
10.description: Horizontal pull-up for beginners. Hang from a low bar with feet on the ground and pull your chest to the bar.
10.instructions:
Set a bar at about waist height
Hang underneath the bar with arms extended
Keep your body straight from heels to head
Pull your chest to the bar squeezing your shoulder blades
Touch the bar with your chest at the top
Lower in a controlled manner until arms are extended

11.name: Diamond Push Up
11.description: Push-ups with hands together forming a diamond shape. Greater emphasis on triceps than regular push-ups.
11.instructions:
Place your hands together on the ground forming a diamond with your fingers
Adopt plank position with body straight
Keep your elbows close to your body during the movement
Lower your chest toward your hands in a controlled manner
Touch your hands with your chest if possible
Push up until arms are extended

12.name: Chin Up
12.description: Pull-up with supinated grip. Similar to pull-up but with palms facing you, greater emphasis on biceps.
12.instructions:
Grab the bar with palms facing you at shoulder width
Hang with arms fully extended
Retract your shoulder blades before initiating the pull
Pull until your chin clears the bar
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement
Lower in a controlled manner to full extension

13.name: Burpee
13.description: Full body exercise. Combines a squat, plank, push-up and jump in one continuous movement.
13.instructions:
Start standing with feet shoulder-width apart
Lower to squat position and place hands on the ground
Jump your feet back to plank position
Perform a complete push-up
Jump your feet toward your hands
Jump explosively upward with arms extended

14.name: Front Lever
14.description: Horizontal position hanging from the bar. Keep your body completely horizontal facing up.
14.instructions:
Hang from the bar with overhand grip at shoulder width
Retract your shoulder blades and depress your shoulders
Strongly engage your lats and core
Raise your hips while keeping arms straight
Extend your body until completely horizontal
Maintain the position with tension throughout your body

15.name: Back Lever
15.description: Inverted horizontal position on the bar. Keep your body horizontal facing down.
15.instructions:
Hang from the bar or rings with overhand grip
Raise your legs and pass between your arms to inverted position
Slowly lower your body toward horizontal
Keep your arms straight and core very engaged
Extend your body until parallel to the ground
Maintain the position controlling your breathing

16.name: Human Flag
16.description: Human flag. Keep your body horizontal while holding a vertical pole.
16.instructions:
Grab a vertical pole with upper hand in overhand grip
Place lower hand in underhand grip below
Push with the lower arm and pull with the upper
Raise your legs laterally toward horizontal
Keep your body straight like a plank
Maintain the position with maximum tension in core and shoulders

17.name: Archer Push Up
17.description: Archer push-up. One hand close to the body while the other extends laterally.
17.instructions:
Adopt push-up position with hands very wide apart
Turn the fingers of one hand outward
Lower your body toward the normally placed hand
Fully extend the other arm to the side
Keep your body straight throughout the movement
Push up and repeat alternating sides

18.name: Tuck Planche
18.description: Planche with tucked knees. Balance on hands with body elevated and knees to chest.
18.instructions:
Place your hands on the ground at shoulder width
Lean forward loading weight onto your hands
Lift your feet off the ground tucking knees to chest
Keep your elbows locked and shoulders protracted
Balance the weight on your hands with core engaged
Hold the position as long as possible

19.name: Dragon Flag
19.description: Advanced core exercise. Lying face up, raise legs and hips keeping only shoulders in contact with the bench.
19.instructions:
Lie face up on a bench holding behind your head
Raise your legs and hips forming a straight line
Only your shoulders should remain in contact with the bench
Slowly lower your body maintaining the straight line
Don't let your lower back touch the bench
Raise back up with control using core strength

20.name: Hanging Leg Raise
20.description: Hanging leg raise. Hang from a bar and raise straight legs until forming a 90-degree angle.
20.instructions:
Hang from a bar with arms extended
Keep your body stable without swinging
Engage your core and hip flexors
Raise your straight legs until parallel to the ground
Hold the position for a second at the top
Lower your legs in a controlled manner

21.name: Wall Push Up
21.description: Push-up against the wall. The most basic exercise in the push-up progression, ideal for absolute beginners.
21.instructions:
Stand facing a wall at arm's length distance
Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height
Keep your body straight from head to heels
Bend your elbows bringing your chest toward the wall
Keep your elbows at 45 degrees from your body
Push back until arms are extended

22.name: Incline Push Up
22.description: Incline push-up with hands on elevated surface. Reduces load compared to standard push-up.
22.instructions:
Place your hands on an elevated surface like a bench or step
Adopt plank position with body straight
Keep your feet on the ground and core engaged
Lower your chest toward the surface by bending your elbows
Keep your elbows at 45 degrees from your body
Push up until arms are extended

23.name: Knee Push Up
23.description: Push-up with knees supported. Modified version that reduces body load by approximately 50%.
23.instructions:
Place your hands on the ground at shoulder width
Support your knees on the ground with ankles crossed
Maintain a straight line from knees to head
Lower your chest toward the ground by bending your elbows
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement
Push up until arms are extended

24.name: Wide Push Up
24.description: Push-up with hands wider than shoulder width. Greater emphasis on chest.
24.instructions:
Place your hands on the ground wider than shoulder width
Adopt plank position with body straight
Slightly turn your fingers outward
Lower your chest toward the ground keeping elbows flared
Feel the stretch in your chest at the bottom
Push up until arms are extended

25.name: One Arm Push Up
25.description: One-arm push-up. Advanced exercise requiring great strength and core stability.
25.instructions:
Adopt push-up position with feet wider than normal
Place one hand in the center of your chest and the other on your back
Keep your core extremely engaged to avoid rotating
Lower your chest toward the ground in a controlled manner
Keep your hips level without rotating
Push up with explosive force

26.name: Scapular Pull Up
26.description: Scapular activation hanging from the bar. First step to build pulling strength.
26.instructions:
Hang from the bar with arms fully extended
Keep your arms straight throughout the exercise
Retract your shoulder blades pulling shoulders down and back
Raise your body a few inches using only scapular movement
Hold the contracted position for a second
Relax your shoulder blades returning to starting position

27.name: Negative Pull Up
27.description: Negative pull-up. Jump up and slowly lower controlling the movement.
27.instructions:
Use a box or jump to reach the top position
Start with your chin above the bar
Lower your body as slowly as possible (5-10 seconds)
Control the movement throughout the descent
Keep your shoulder blades retracted as you lower
Reach full extension and repeat

28.name: Band Assisted Pull Up
28.description: Band-assisted pull-up. The band reduces the body weight you need to lift.
28.instructions:
Place a resistance band on the bar
Put one foot or knee in the band
Hang with arms extended
Perform the pull-up with band assistance
Rise until your chin clears the bar
Lower in a controlled manner using the resistance

29.name: Weighted Pull Up
29.description: Weighted pull-up. Advanced progression to increase pulling strength.
29.instructions:
Wear a weight belt with weight or hold a dumbbell between your feet
Hang from the bar with arms extended
Perform the pull-up with the additional weight
Maintain control throughout the movement
Rise until your chin clears the bar
Lower in a controlled manner without swinging

30.name: Assisted Squat
30.description: Assisted squat holding onto something. Ideal for learning proper technique.
30.instructions:
Stand facing a stable support you can grip
Hold the support with your hands at chest height
Perform the squat using the support for balance
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground
Use the support as little as necessary
Rise by pushing through your heels

31.name: Box Squat
31.description: Squat to a box or bench. Helps control depth and technique.
31.instructions:
Place a box or bench behind you at desired height
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Lower in a controlled manner until you sit on the box
Maintain tension without completely relaxing
Pause briefly on the box
Push through your heels to stand up

32.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
32.description: Bulgarian split squat with rear foot elevated. Works each leg unilaterally.
32.instructions:
Place the top of your rear foot on a bench behind you
Step forward with your front foot
Keep your torso upright throughout the movement
Lower until your rear knee almost touches the ground
Keep your front knee aligned with your foot
Push through your front heel to rise

33.name: Shrimp Squat
33.description: Shrimp squat. Advanced single-leg squat variation with rear leg held.
33.instructions:
Stand on one leg
Hold the foot of your free leg with the same-side hand behind you
Keep your chest up and core engaged
Lower until your rear knee almost touches the ground
Maintain balance throughout the movement
Push through your heel to return to the top

34.name: Bench Dips
34.description: Bench dips. Easier version of dips using a bench or chair.
34.instructions:
Sit on the edge of a bench with hands at your sides
Slide your bottom off the bench with legs extended
Lower your body by bending elbows to 90 degrees
Keep your back close to the bench during the movement
Push up until arms are extended
Keep shoulders away from your ears

35.name: Assisted Dips
35.description: Band or machine assisted dips. Reduces body load to build strength.
35.instructions:
Place a resistance band on the parallel bars
Place your knees or feet in the band for assistance
Grip the bars with arms extended
Lower your body by bending elbows to 90 degrees
The band will help push you up
Maintain control throughout the movement

36.name: Ring Dips
36.description: Ring dips. Requires greater stability and strength than parallel bar dips.
36.instructions:
Grip the rings and push up to support position
Turn the rings out (RTO) for greater activation
Keep the rings stable close to your body
Lower by bending elbows to 90 degrees
Maintain control of the rings throughout the movement
Push up to full extension

37.name: Weighted Dips
37.description: Weighted dips. Progression to increase pushing strength.
37.instructions:
Wear a weight belt with additional weight
Grip the parallel bars with arms extended
Keep your core engaged and body controlled
Lower your body by bending elbows to 90 degrees
Push up until arms are extended
Keep the weight stable without swinging

38.name: Incline Plank
38.description: Incline plank with hands on elevated surface. Easier version of the plank.
38.instructions:
Place your hands on an elevated surface like a bench
Extend your legs back in plank position
Keep your body straight from head to heels
Engage your core by squeezing your abs
Keep your shoulders over your hands
Hold the position breathing normally

39.name: Side Plank
39.description: Side plank. Works obliques and lateral core stability.
39.instructions:
Lie on your side supporting yourself on your forearm
Raise your hips forming a straight line
Keep your elbow directly under your shoulder
Engage your obliques to maintain the position
You can stack your feet or stagger them for balance
Maintain the position without letting your hips drop

40.name: Plank with Leg Lift
40.description: Plank with leg raise. Increases core stability demand.
40.instructions:
Adopt plank position on forearms
Keep your body straight and core engaged
Raise one leg straight without rotating your hips
Hold the raised leg for a few seconds
Lower the leg with control
Alternate with the other leg

41.name: High Pull Up
41.description: High pull-up bringing bar to chest or lower. Prepares for muscle up.
41.instructions:
Hang from the bar with overhand grip
Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades
Pull explosively bringing the bar to chest or sternum
Keep your elbows back during the pull
Touch the bar as low as possible on your torso
Lower in a controlled manner to extension

42.name: Explosive Pull Up
42.description: Explosive pull-up with flight phase. Develops power needed for muscle up.
42.instructions:
Hang from the bar with overhand grip
Pull explosively with maximum power
Release the bar at the top of the movement
Raise your hands above the bar briefly
Re-grab the bar on the descent
Lower in a controlled manner and repeat

43.name: Tucked L-Sit
43.description: L-Sit with tucked knees. First progression toward full L-Sit.
43.instructions:
Sit on the ground or between parallettes
Place your hands beside your hips
Press against the ground and lift your body
Tuck your knees toward your chest
Hold the position with core engaged
Try to gradually straighten your legs

44.name: V-Sit
44.description: V position with legs raised above horizontal. Advanced L-Sit progression.
44.instructions:
Adopt L-Sit position with legs extended
Raise your legs above horizontal
Lean your torso slightly back for balance
Keep your arms straight and locked
Strongly engage your hip flexors
Hold the position forming a V shape

45.name: Pike Push Up
45.description: Pike push-up. Simulates handstand push-up movement with less load.
45.instructions:
Adopt an inverted V position with hands and feet on the ground
Keep your legs as straight as possible
Lower your head toward the ground by bending your elbows
Keep your hips elevated throughout the movement
Gently touch the ground with your head
Push up until arms are extended

46.name: Elevated Pike Push Up
46.description: Pike push-up with elevated feet. Greater shoulder load than normal pike.
46.instructions:
Place your feet on an elevated surface like a box
Adopt pike position with hips elevated
Keep your legs straight with feet on the box
Lower your head toward the ground
Keep your elbows pointing back
Push up to extension

47.name: Wall Handstand Push Up
47.description: Wall handstand push-up. Assisted version of freestanding handstand push-up.
47.instructions:
Place your hands 6-8 inches from the wall
Kick up to handstand with feet on the wall
Keep your core tight and body straight
Lower your head toward the ground by bending your elbows
Keep your elbows pointing forward
Push up until arms are extended

48.name: Dead Bug
48.description: Core exercise lying face up moving arms and legs alternately.
48.instructions:
Lie face up with arms extended toward the ceiling
Raise your legs with knees at 90 degrees
Press your lower back against the floor
Extend one arm back and the opposite leg forward
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor
Return to center and alternate with the other side

49.name: Hollow Body Hold
49.description: Hollow position with lower back pressed to floor. Fundamental for gymnastics.
49.instructions:
Lie face up with arms extended overhead
Raise your shoulders and legs off the ground
Press your lower back firmly against the floor
Keep your arms next to your ears
Keep your legs straight and together
Hold the position without losing the hollow shape

50.name: Knee Raise
50.description: Hanging knee raise. Easier version of hanging leg raise.
50.instructions:
Hang from a bar with arms extended
Keep your body stable without swinging
Raise your knees toward your chest
Contract your core at the top
Lower your legs in a controlled manner
Avoid using momentum or swinging

51.name: Toes to Bar
51.description: Bring feet to bar while hanging. Advanced leg raise progression.
51.instructions:
Hang from the bar with overhand grip
Initiate a slight controlled kip or swing
Raise your straight legs toward the bar
Touch the bar with your feet
Lower your legs in a controlled manner
Maintain rhythm for subsequent repetitions

52.name: Tuck Front Lever
52.description: Front lever with knees tucked to chest. First front lever progression.
52.instructions:
Hang from the bar with overhand grip
Retract your shoulder blades and depress your shoulders
Tuck your knees toward your chest
Raise your hips until horizontal
Keep your arms straight and lats engaged
Hold the position as long as possible

53.name: Advanced Tuck Front Lever
53.description: Front lever with slightly extended knees. Intermediate progression.
53.instructions:
From tuck front lever, extend your hips
Keep your knees bent but away from your chest
Your body should form a more open position
Keep your arms straight and lats engaged
Keep your hips at shoulder height
Hold the position working toward extension

54.name: Straddle Front Lever
54.description: Front lever with legs spread. Advanced progression toward full front lever.
54.instructions:
From front lever position, spread your legs
Keep your legs straight and open in straddle
Keep your body horizontal with arms straight
Strongly engage your lats and core
Keep your hips aligned with your shoulders
Work toward bringing your legs together gradually

55.name: Tuck Back Lever
55.description: Back lever with tucked knees. First back lever progression.
55.instructions:
Hang from rings or bar and pass to inverted position
Lower your body back keeping knees to chest
Keep your arms straight during the descent
Stop when body is horizontal with knees tucked
Keep shoulders active and core tight
Hold the position with control

56.name: Straddle Back Lever
56.description: Back lever with legs spread. Progression toward full back lever.
56.instructions:
From tuck back lever, extend your hips
Open your legs in straddle position
Keep your body horizontal facing down
Keep your arms straight and shoulders active
Engage your core to maintain the position
Work toward bringing your legs together

57.name: Planche Lean
57.description: Planche lean in push-up position. Develops pushing strength.
57.instructions:
Adopt plank position with arms extended
Protract your shoulders pushing the floor away
Lean forward loading weight onto your hands
Keep your elbows locked
Your shoulders should pass in front of your wrists
Hold the position working the lean

58.name: Straddle Planche
58.description: Planche with legs spread. Advanced progression toward full planche.
58.instructions:
From tuck planche, extend your hips
Open your legs in straddle position
Keep your arms straight and locked
Protract your shoulders to the maximum
Keep your body parallel to the ground
Keep your legs active and extended

59.name: Full Planche
59.description: Full planche with legs together and extended. One of the most difficult exercises.
59.instructions:
Start in straddle planche if necessary
Slowly bring your legs together maintaining balance
Keep your legs straight and together
Your arms must be completely locked
Protract your shoulders and engage your core to the maximum
Keep your body perfectly horizontal

60.name: Nordic Curl
60.description: Advanced hamstring exercise. Kneel with feet anchored and lower your body toward the ground controlling the movement with your hamstrings.
60.instructions:
Kneel with your feet anchored under something stable
Keep your hips extended and core engaged
Lower your torso toward the ground in a controlled manner
Use only your hamstrings to control the descent
Lower as far as you can before using your hands
Push with your hands and contract your hamstrings to rise

61.name: Calf Raises
61.description: Basic calf exercise. Standing, raise your heels off the ground contracting your calves and lower in a controlled manner.
61.instructions:
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
You can use a wall for balance if needed
Raise your heels off the ground going onto your toes
Contract your calves at the top
Hold the position for a second
Lower your heels in a controlled manner

62.name: Windshield Wipers
62.description: Advanced rotational core exercise. Hanging from the bar, raise your legs and rotate them side to side while maintaining control.
62.instructions:
Hang from the bar with wide overhand grip
Raise your straight legs to the bar
Keep your legs together and straight
Rotate your legs to one side in an arc
Control the movement with your obliques
Rotate to the other side completing the windshield wiper

63.name: German Hang
63.description: Mobility position on rings or low bar. Hang with arms behind your body stretching shoulders and chest.
63.instructions:
Hang from rings or a low bar
Pass your legs between your arms forward
Lower until your arms are behind your body
Keep your arms straight during the stretch
Feel the stretch in your shoulders and chest
Hold the position breathing deeply

64.name: Handstand
64.description: Inverted balance on hands. Keep your body straight and aligned while supporting yourself upside down.
64.instructions:
Place your hands on the ground at shoulder width
Kick up to inverted position with momentum or from strength
Keep your arms completely extended
Squeeze your core and glutes
Look between your hands for balance
Keep your body in a straight line from wrists to feet

65.name: Pseudo Planche Push Up
65.description: Push-up with hands at hip level and body leaning forward. Prepares for the planche.
65.instructions:
Adopt push-up position with hands next to your hips
Turn your fingers toward your feet or outward
Lean forward loading weight onto your hands
Lower your body by bending your elbows
Maintain the forward lean during the movement
Push up maintaining the leaned position

66.name: Archer Pull Up
66.description: Unilateral pull-up with one arm extended laterally. Transfers more load to one side of the body.
66.instructions:
Grab the bar with wide grip
Pull toward one side bringing your chest to that hand
Fully extend the other arm to the side
Keep the extended arm straight during the pull
Lower in a controlled manner to center
Repeat toward the other side

67.name: One Arm Pull Up
67.description: Complete pull-up using only one arm. One of the most advanced pulling exercises in calisthenics.
67.instructions:
Hang from the bar with one arm
You can use your other arm on your wrist for initial assistance
Engage your shoulder blade before pulling
Pull forcefully bringing your chin over the bar
Keep your body controlled without excessive rotation
Lower in a controlled manner to extension

68.name: Clap Push Up
68.description: Explosive plyometric push-up. Push forcefully to lift your hands off the ground and clap before landing.
68.instructions:
Adopt standard push-up position
Lower your body toward the ground
Push explosively to lift your entire body
Clap your hands in the air
Land softly with elbows slightly bent
Absorb the impact and continue to the next repetition

69.name: Korean Dips
69.description: Dips with hands behind the body on a low bar. Intensely works the triceps and shoulders.
69.instructions:
Place your hands on a low bar behind your body
Your fingers should point forward
Lower your body by bending elbows back
Keep your elbows pointing back, not out
Lower until you feel a good stretch
Push up until arms are extended

70.name: One Leg Front Lever
70.description: Front lever with one leg extended and the other tucked. Advanced progression toward full front lever.
70.instructions:
From tuck front lever, extend one leg
Keep the other leg tucked to your chest
Keep your body horizontal with arms straight
Engage your lats and core to the maximum
Alternate the extended leg between sets
Work toward extending both legs

71.name: Advanced Tuck Planche
71.description: Planche with hips extended but knees still tucked. Progression between tuck planche and straddle planche.
71.instructions:
From tuck planche, extend your hips
Keep your knees bent but away from your body
Your body should be more horizontal than in tuck
Keep arms locked and shoulders protracted
Strongly engage your core
Work toward full leg extension

72.name: Bicycle with Band
72.description: Core exercise with bicycle movement using a resistance band. Strengthens the abdominals and hip flexors.
72.instructions:
Lie on your back with the band hooked around your feet
Raise your legs with knees at 90 degrees
Bring one knee to your chest while extending the other
Rotate your torso bringing the opposite elbow toward the rising knee
Alternate the movement in a continuous controlled manner
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise

73.name: Pull Over with Band
73.description: Back and shoulder exercise with a band anchored above. Works the lats through their full range of motion.
73.instructions:
Anchor the band at a high point behind you
Lie down or sit facing the anchor point
Grab the band with arms extended overhead
Pull the band bringing your arms toward your thighs
Keep your arms slightly bent during the movement
Return slowly to the starting position controlling the resistance

74.name: Chest Press with Band
74.description: Chest press variation with resistance band. Activates chest, shoulders and triceps with progressive resistance.
74.instructions:
Anchor the band behind you or at a low point
Hold the band with both hands at chest height
Push forward fully extending your arms
Keep elbows at 45 degrees from your body during the movement
Control the return without letting the band pull you back abruptly
Repeat keeping your core engaged

75.name: Lunge Fly
75.description: Combines a lunge with a chest fly using a resistance band. Works legs and chest simultaneously.
75.instructions:
Anchor the band behind you at chest height
Grab the ends with both hands
Step forward into a lunge
As you lower, open your arms laterally like a chest fly
Rise from the lunge closing your arms at the front
Alternate legs between repetitions

76.name: Bicep Curl Low Anchor
76.description: Bicep curl with band anchored below. Works the biceps with constant resistance throughout the range of motion.
76.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends with palms facing up
Keep your elbows close to your body
Bend your elbows raising your hands toward your shoulders
Control the descent slowly
Avoid swinging your body during the movement

77.name: Curl Press
77.description: Combination of bicep curl and shoulder press with a band. Compound exercise for arms and shoulders.
77.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet
Start with arms extended and palms facing forward
Perform a bicep curl bringing your hands to your shoulders
Without pausing, press your arms overhead
Lower your arms in a controlled manner to the starting position
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement

78.name: Shoulder Press with Band
78.description: Shoulder press with resistance band. Works the deltoids and triceps with adjustable resistance.
78.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends at shoulder height with elbows bent
Push upward fully extending your arms
Your arms should end slightly in front of your ears
Lower in a controlled manner to the starting position
Keep your back straight and core engaged

79.name: Calf Raise with Band
79.description: Calf raise with band resistance. Strengthens the calves with additional load.
79.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet
Pass the band over your shoulders or hold the ends at your sides
Stand with feet at shoulder width
Raise your heels going on your toes contracting your calves
Hold the top position for a second
Lower your heels in a controlled manner

80.name: Russian Twist with Band
80.description: Russian twist with resistance band. Works the obliques and rotational core.
80.instructions:
Sit on the ground with knees slightly bent
Anchor the band to one side at torso height
Grab the band with both hands in front of you
Rotate your torso toward the opposite side of the anchor
Resist the tension back controlling the movement
Alternate the anchor point to work both sides

81.name: Lat Pull with Band
81.description: Lat pull-down with band anchored above. Simulates the lat pull-down machine to work the back.
81.instructions:
Anchor the band at a high point above your head
Sit or kneel facing the anchor
Grab the band with both hands wider than shoulder width
Pull the band toward your chest or chin
Keep your elbows pointing down and back
Return slowly to the starting position with arms extended

82.name: Chest Fly with Band
82.description: Chest fly with resistance band. Works the chest through a wide range of motion with constant resistance.
82.instructions:
Anchor the band behind you at chest height
Grab the ends with arms extended to the sides
Bring your hands together in front slightly crossing if possible
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement
Open your arms back controlling the resistance
Feel the stretch in your chest in the open position

83.name: Jumping Jacks with Band
83.description: Jumping jacks with resistance band at your feet. Increases resistance and muscle recruitment of the classic exercise.
83.instructions:
Place the band around your ankles or feet
Start with feet together and arms at your sides
Jump opening your feet beyond shoulder width against the resistance
Raise your arms laterally until overhead
Jump back to the starting position
Maintain a consistent controlled rhythm

84.name: Tricep Extension with Band
84.description: Tricep extension with anchored band. Isolates the tricep with adjustable resistance.
84.instructions:
Anchor the band at a high point in front of you
Grab the band with both hands palms facing down
Keep your elbows close to your head and together
Extend your elbows downward pushing the band
Reach full extension contracting your tricep
Return slowly to the starting position without moving your elbows

85.name: Lunge Front Raise
85.description: Combines a lunge with a frontal arm raise using a band. Works legs and shoulders at the same time.
85.instructions:
Step on the band with your front lunge foot
Grab the other end with both hands in front of your thighs
Lower into a lunge while raising your arms forward to shoulder height
Keep your arms straight during the raise
Rise from the lunge lowering your arms in a controlled manner
Alternate legs between repetitions

86.name: Upright Row with Band
86.description: Upright row with resistance band. Works shoulders and upper back.
86.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends with overhand grip hands close together
Pull the band upward to your chin
Keep your elbows above your hands during the movement
Your shoulders should rise slightly at the end of the range
Lower in a controlled manner to the starting position

87.name: Back Squat with Band
87.description: Squat with resistance band over the shoulders. Adds resistance to the classic squat for greater muscle activation.
87.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Pass the band over your shoulders holding it securely
Squat as normal keeping your back straight
Your knees should follow your foot line
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground
Push through your heels to rise against the resistance

88.name: Cross Plank with Band
88.description: Plank variation with resistance band that works anti-rotational core stability.
88.instructions:
Start in a high plank position with the band tied to one wrist
The other end of the band is anchored to one side
Maintain a stable plank position without rotating
Extend the arm with the band forward fighting against rotation
Keep your hips level and core very engaged
Bring your arm back and repeat on the other side

89.name: Tricep Kickback with Band
89.description: Tricep kickback with resistance band. Extend your elbow against the resistance to work the tricep.
89.instructions:
Anchor the band behind you at torso height
Lean forward with your back almost parallel to the ground
Grab the band with one arm and elbow bent at 90 degrees
Fully extend your elbow back
Control the return without letting the band pull your arm back abruptly
Repeat and switch arms

90.name: Lunge Press
90.description: Combination of lunge and shoulder press with a band. Compound exercise that works the whole body.
90.instructions:
Step on the band with your front lunge foot
Grab the ends at shoulder height
Lower into a lunge at the same time you press overhead
Fully extend your arms at the bottom of the lunge
Rise from the lunge lowering your arms in a controlled manner
Alternate legs between repetitions

91.name: L Raise with Band
91.description: Lateral and frontal raise in an L pattern using a resistance band. Works all three deltoid heads.
91.instructions:
Step on the band with the foot of the same side arm
Grab the end with your hand
Raise your arm laterally to shoulder height
Hold for a moment
Lower and repeat the frontal raise to shoulder height
Alternate between lateral and frontal or do them in one L-shaped movement

92.name: Lunge with Band
92.description: Classic lunge with resistance band at your feet. Adds resistance for greater glute and quad activation.
92.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet
Grab the ends at the sides of your body
Step forward into a lunge
Lower until your rear knee almost touches the ground
Keep your torso upright and core engaged
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position

93.name: Oblique Twist with Band
93.description: Oblique twist with anchored band. Works the obliques with angular resistance to strengthen rotational core.
93.instructions:
Anchor the band to one side at shoulder height
Grab the band with both hands in front of you
Rotate your torso downward bringing your hands toward the opposite hip
Control the movement back to the starting position
Complete all reps on one side before switching
Keep your arms almost extended during the rotation

94.name: Bicep Curl High Anchor
94.description: Bicep curl with band anchored above. Changes the angle of resistance for greater muscle activation.
94.instructions:
Anchor the band at a high point in front of or beside you
Grab the ends with arms extended toward the anchor
Keep your elbows elevated at shoulder height
Bend your elbows toward your head contracting your biceps
Keep your elbows still throughout the movement
Return slowly to the starting position

95.name: Squat Clean with Band
95.description: Combination of squat and clean with resistance band. High-intensity adapted Olympic exercise.
95.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends at knee height
Perform a deep squat keeping your back straight
As you rise explosively, pull the band to your shoulders
Your hands should reach the rack position at your shoulders
Absorb the movement by slightly bending your knees

96.name: Arm Circles with Band
96.description: Arm circles with resistance band. Warm-up and mobility exercise that activates the shoulders.
96.instructions:
Hold the band with both hands wider than shoulder width
Keep your arms extended in front of you
Make large circles with your arms passing the band overhead
Return passing the band behind your body
Maintain constant tension in the band throughout
Alternate the direction of the circles

97.name: Hamstring Curl with Band
97.description: Hamstring curl with resistance band. Works the hamstrings with adjustable resistance.
97.instructions:
Anchor the band at a low point in front of you
Place the band around one ankle
Lie face down with the anchor toward your feet
Bend your knee bringing your heel toward your glutes
Resist the tension back controlling the descent
Repeat and switch legs

98.name: Crunches with Band
98.description: Abdominal crunch with resistance band. Increases the intensity of classic crunches.
98.instructions:
Anchor the band at a high point behind your head
Lie on your back holding the band over your shoulders
Flex your torso bringing your chest toward your knees
Contract your abs at the top of the movement
Slowly lower controlling the band resistance
Do not use the band momentum to rise

99.name: Band Row
99.description: Row with resistance band anchored in front. Works the mid-back muscles and biceps.
99.instructions:
Anchor the band at medium height in front of you
Grab the ends with both hands and step back
Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back straight
Pull the band toward your abdomen squeezing your shoulder blades
Keep your elbows close to your body during the movement
Return slowly to the starting position with arms extended

100.name: Band Resisted Push Up
100.description: Push-ups with resistance band adding difficulty. Significantly increases the challenge of the classic push-up.
100.instructions:
Pass the band behind your back holding the ends with each hand
Adopt a high plank position
Lower your chest toward the ground as in a normal push-up
Push up overcoming the additional band resistance
Keep your body straight throughout the movement
The band should be taut in the top position

101.name: High Knees with Band
101.description: High knees with resistance band at your feet. Works legs and core with additional resistance.
101.instructions:
Place the band around your feet or ankles
Start standing with feet at shoulder width
Raise one knee toward your chest overcoming the resistance
Alternate your knees quickly in continuous movement
Keep your torso upright and arms moving naturally
Maintain a consistent pace and straight back

102.name: Diamond Push Up with Band
102.description: Diamond push-up with resistance band adding extra load. Greater tricep emphasis with additional resistance.
102.instructions:
Pass the band behind your back
Place your hands on the ground in a diamond shape and hold the band ends
Adopt a plank position with body straight
Lower your chest toward your hands keeping elbows close to body
Push up overcoming the additional resistance
Maintain the diamond position throughout the movement

103.name: Thruster with Band
103.description: Squat and shoulder press in one continuous movement with a band. High-intensity full body exercise.
103.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends at shoulder height
Lower into a deep squat keeping your back straight
As you rise explosively, perform a shoulder press in the same movement
Fully extend your arms overhead
Lower your arms at the pace of the next squat

104.name: Deltoid Fly
104.description: Lateral deltoid fly with resistance band. Works the lateral deltoid in isolation.
104.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends with arms extended at your sides
Raise your arms laterally to shoulder height
Keep a slight bend in your elbows during the movement
Your thumbs should point slightly downward
Lower your arms in a controlled manner

105.name: Front Squat with Band
105.description: Front squat with resistance band. Greater quad activation than the back squat.
105.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Cross the band over your chest or hold the ends at your shoulders
Keep your elbows elevated in front of you throughout
Lower into a deep squat keeping your torso very upright
Your knees should follow your foot line
Push through your heels to rise

106.name: Heel Touches
106.description: Heel touches with band resistance. Works the obliques and lateral abdomen.
106.instructions:
Anchor the band at lateral shoulder height when lying down
Lie on your back with knees bent
Grab the band end with the same side hand
Raise your shoulder off the ground laterally touching your heel
Return slowly controlling the resistance
Repeat on the same side then switch

107.name: Romanian Deadlift with Band
107.description: Romanian deadlift with resistance band. Works the hamstrings and glutes with progressive resistance.
107.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet at shoulder width
Grab the ends with both hands in front of your thighs
Keep your knees slightly bent
Hinge forward pushing your hips back while keeping your back straight
Keep the band close to your legs throughout
Contract your glutes and hamstrings to return to standing

108.name: Spiderman Push Up with Band
108.description: Spiderman push-up with resistance band. Combines push-up with hip rotation to work chest and core.
108.instructions:
Pass the band behind your back holding the ends
Adopt a high plank position
As you lower in the push-up, bring one knee toward the elbow on the same side
Return your leg to plank position as you rise
Alternate legs each repetition
Keep your core very engaged throughout

109.name: Lunge Row
109.description: Combination of lunge with back row using a band. Compound exercise that works legs and back.
109.instructions:
Anchor the band at medium height in front of you
Grab the ends and step back into a lunge
At the bottom of the lunge, perform a row pulling toward your abdomen
Keep your back straight during both movements
Return to standing releasing the row in a controlled manner
Alternate legs between repetitions

110.name: Side Squat with Band
110.description: Side or sumo squat with resistance band. Works the inner thighs and glutes.
110.instructions:
Place the band around your ankles or feet
Open your feet in a sumo position wider than shoulder width
Lower into a squat with feet open and back straight
Your knees should follow the direction of your feet
Push against the band resistance as you open your feet
Rise by pushing through your heels

111.name: Flutter Kick with Band
111.description: Flutter kick with resistance band at your ankles. Works the lower core with additional resistance.
111.instructions:
Place the band around your ankles
Lie on your back with hands under your glutes
Raise both legs about 6 inches off the ground
Alternate your legs up and down in small ranges
Keep your legs straight against the band resistance
Keep your core engaged and lower back pressed to the floor

112.name: High Row with Band
112.description: High row with band to shoulder level. Works the trapezius and upper back.
112.instructions:
Anchor the band at a low point in front of you
Grab the ends with arms extended downward
Pull the band upward bringing your hands to chest height
Keep your elbows above your hands during the pull
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top of the movement
Lower slowly to the starting position

113.name: Clap Push Up with Band
113.description: Explosive clap push-up with resistance band. Combines plyometrics with additional resistance.
113.instructions:
Pass the band behind your back holding the ends
Adopt a push-up position
Lower your body toward the floor in a controlled manner
Push explosively overcoming the band resistance
Raise your hands off the ground and clap quickly
Land softly with elbows slightly bent

114.name: Squat Row
114.description: Combination of squat and row with resistance band. Compound exercise for legs and back.
114.instructions:
Anchor the band at medium height in front of you
Grab the ends and step back to add tension to the band
Lower into a squat while extending your arms toward the anchor
As you rise from the squat, perform a row pulling toward your abdomen
Coordinate the pull with the leg extension
Keep your back straight throughout

115.name: X Arm Extension
115.description: Crossed arm extension with a band. Works chest, back and shoulders in a diagonal movement.
115.instructions:
Hold the band crossed with each hand grabbing the opposite end
Start with arms crossed in front of your chest
Extend your arms diagonally outward forming an X
Keep a slight bend in your elbows during the movement
Control the close returning to the crossed position
Feel the activation in your chest, back and shoulders

116.name: Squat Twist
116.description: Squat combined with trunk rotation using a band. Works legs and rotational core.
116.instructions:
Anchor the band to one side at chest height
Grab with both hands and step away to add tension
Lower into a squat keeping your hands in front of your chest
As you rise, rotate your torso toward the opposite side of the anchor
Return to center before lowering into the next rep
Complete all reps on one side before switching

117.name: Pike Push Up with Band
117.description: Pike push-up with resistance band adding load. Greater shoulder challenge in the inverted position.
117.instructions:
Pass the band behind your back holding the ends
Adopt an inverted V position with hips elevated
Keep your legs as straight as possible
Lower your head toward the ground bending your elbows
Keep your hips elevated throughout the movement
Push up overcoming the resistance until arms are extended

118.name: Split Squat with Band
118.description: Split squat with resistance band under your feet. Works each leg unilaterally with additional resistance.
118.instructions:
Step on the band with both feet in a split position
Grab the ends at the sides of your body
Lower until your rear knee almost touches the ground
Keep your torso upright and core engaged
Your front knee should follow your foot line
Push through your front heel to rise

119.name: Anti-Rotation Crunch
119.description: Crunch with anti-rotational band resistance. Works core stability against rotational forces.
119.instructions:
Anchor the band to one side at shoulder height when lying down
Lie on your back with knees bent
Grab the band with both hands over your chest
Perform a normal crunch while resisting the rotation the band creates
Keep your shoulders parallel to the ground during the crunch
Lower slowly controlling the resistance

120.name: Pistol Squat with Band
120.description: Band-assisted pistol squat. The band reduces the load to help learn the pistol squat technique.
120.instructions:
Anchor the band at a high point in front of you
Grab the band with both hands for assistance
Stand on one leg with the other extended forward
Lower into a squat using the band to help with balance and load
Lower until your glute almost touches your heel
Push through your heel to rise using less assistance each time

121.name: Knees to Chest
121.description: Knees to chest raise with band resistance. Works the hip flexors and core.
121.instructions:
Place the band around your feet
Sit on the ground with legs extended
Support yourself on your hands behind your hips
Bring your knees toward your chest overcoming the band resistance
Control the extension back without letting the band carry you
Keep your core engaged throughout

122.name: Levitating Lunge
122.description: Levitating lunge with resistance band. Advanced lunge variation that works balance and glutes.
122.instructions:
Place the band around your ankles
Start standing on one leg
Lower into a lunge with your supporting leg while keeping the other suspended
The free leg does not touch the ground at any point
Maintain your balance using your core and glutes
Rise with control returning to the standing position

123.name: Leg Raise with Band
123.description: Leg raise with resistance band. Works the lower core with greater difficulty.
123.instructions:
Place the band around your feet or ankles
Lie on your back with hands under your glutes
Keep your legs straight and together
Raise both legs to 90 degrees against the band resistance
Hold for a second at the top
Lower slowly controlling the resistance without resting your feet on the ground
